Only on your device — Milesta has no account and no server of its own. That also means: if you delete the app, your journal goes with it, so keep a backup: export one any time, or turn on automatic monthly backups in Settings.
How do I back up my journal?

Settings → Data → <0>Export Backup</0> creates a single file containing every milestone, photo, and category. You can also enable <1>Automatic monthly backup</1>; copies are kept in the Files app under On My iPhone → Milesta.
How do I move to a new iPhone?
Export a backup on the old device, send the file to the new one (AirDrop or Files), install Milesta, then Settings → Data → <0>Import Backup</0>.
Recaps cover completed periods: the June recap appears on July 1, half-year recaps on January 1 and July 1, and the yearly Wrapped on January 1.
Subscriptions are managed by Apple: Settings → your Apple ID → Subscriptions → Milesta → Cancel. Your milestones remain fully accessible on the free tier.
The lock engages when the app goes to the background and on launch. If it appears unlocked, iOS may have kept the app active — swipe it away or lock the phone to force it.
How Milesta handles your data: no account, no ads, no server of our own. Your journal stays on your device, and usage statistics are opt-in and anonymous.
Milesta is a private, local-first life journal for iOS.
Nothing, by default. Milesta has no accounts, no tracking, and no servers operated by us.

If — and only if — you opt in (during onboarding or in Settings), Milesta sends <0>anonymous usage statistics</0> to PostHog, hosted in the European Union: which features are used and how often. These events never contain your milestone texts, notes, photos, places, links, or any identifier tied to you, and you can switch them off at any time in Settings. See <1>PostHog's privacy policy</1>.
Every milestone, photo, note, link, and category you create is stored only on your device, in the app's local database. Deleting the app deletes the data.

If you turn on “Keep in iCloud Drive” in Settings, your automatic monthly backups are saved to your own iCloud Drive, in the Milesta folder, under your Apple Account and Apple's terms. We have no access to them.
Only content you explicitly share yourself:
Recap images, posters, or text summaries you send through the iOS share sheet.
Backup files you export through the Files app.
Automatic backups, if you choose to keep them in your own iCloud Drive.
Milesta never transmits anything on its own. Optional automatic backups stay on your device unless you choose iCloud Drive.

Adding a place to a milestone is optional. If you tap the current-location button, iOS asks for permission and Milesta performs a single lookup to turn your position into a short place name (like "Berlin, Germany"). Only that text is saved, on your device. Milesta never tracks, stores, or transmits coordinates, and never accesses location in the background.
If you enable App Lock, Face ID is evaluated entirely by iOS on your device. Milesta only receives a yes/no result and never accesses biometric data.

Subscriptions are processed by Apple. If enabled, receipt validation is handled by RevenueCat using an anonymous identifier; no personal information or journal content is ever involved. See <0>RevenueCat's privacy policy</0>.
Anniversary reminders, recap announcements, and encouragement notes are scheduled locally on your device. No push servers are used.

Because Milesta stores no personal data on any server, there is nothing for us to access, correct, export, or erase on your behalf — your data is exclusively in your hands, on your device. For any privacy question, contact us using the details in the <0>Impressum</0>.

milesta.app uses PostHog, hosted in the European Union, in <0>cookieless mode</0> for aggregate visit statistics: no cookies, no local storage, no cross-site tracking, and IP addresses are discarded at ingestion. Page performance metrics are collected anonymously via Vercel Speed Insights. Neither can identify you. If you pick a language or pause the animations, your browser remembers that choice on your device; it is never sent to us.

Milesta is a private life journal for people who quit journaling: instead of daily entries, you log the moments that actually matter — a new job, a move, a first marathon — and Milesta renders them as a winding path you scroll through like a hiking trail of your own life. Monthly and yearly recaps become Wrapped-style cards. Everything stays on your iPhone: no account, no ads.

Most journaling apps ask for 200 words a day and lose you by February. Milesta asks for maybe 20 milestones a year — and gives you something beautiful back. Every milestone becomes a waypoint on a winding trail, drawn across the seasons of your life. Tap play and a cinematic story replay turns your journey into a full-screen highlight reel. At the end of every month and every year, Milesta builds Wrapped-style recap cards, posters, and 9:16 story images designed to be shared — your newest monthly recap free, the rest with Premium.

Under the hood, Milesta takes the opposite bet of the big journaling platforms: it is local-first by design. There is no account to create and no server to sync with — your entries live on the device. They are stored locally, protected with Face ID, and backed up however you choose: a one-tap portable export or automatic monthly backups, none of it behind a paywall. Nothing leaves the phone unless you share it or back it up, and anonymous usage statistics are sent only if you opt in. The app ships fully localized in 15 languages — including right-to-left Arabic and Urdu — built end-to-end by one developer in Germany.
